$comment: Two tables, which each SDK that reads the store runs. `cases`: where the launcher's state home is: the directory that holds tokens.json (and the launcher's own stack.json and discovery/kbs.json). Every program that finds those files computes it the same way. `os` is `macos`, `windows`, or anything else; `home` is the home directory (HOME, or USERPROFILE on Windows), `xdgStateHome` is XDG_STATE_HOME, and `localAppData` is LOCALAPPDATA; null, or a key a case leaves out, means not set. `dir` null means there is no state home, and nothing is read or written. `dir` is written with the system's own separator, whatever system computes it: a backslash on Windows, a slash elsewhere. Rust (packages/sdk-rust: sign_in_store::state_dir, in tests/sign_in_store.rs), Python (packages/sdk-python: sign_in_store.state_dir, in tests/test_state_dir.py) and Go (packages/sdk-go: StateDir, in statedir_test.go) each run every case; each is given what the environment says and reads none itself. The launcher finds its state home through Go's, and its StateDir (apps/launcher/internal/launcher/statefile.go) reads the environment for it. `renewals`: what a renewal of a kept sign-in writes and gives, when other programs renew the same stack and sign it out (README.md, Renewing it). A row's store holds `kept` for the stack when the row begins, and its renewer holds the access token `holding`, null for none: the one the gateway refused, or the one due. `meanwhile` is what another program does to the stack's sign-in, null for nothing: it `renews` (its own renewal, or a sign-in again), leaving `theirs`, or it `signs-out`; `before` the renewal reads the store, or `during` the renewal's grant, after its read and before its write. The issuer answers a grant with `issues`, which has no `refreshToken` when the issuer rotates none. `spends` is the refresh token the renewal's grant presents to the issuer, null when it makes no grant; a runner fails a renewal that makes more than one. `leaves` is what the store then holds for the stack, null for nothing, and `gives` the access token the renewal gives its holder, null for none. A sign-in here is its `token` and its `refreshToken`; a runner keeps the rest as a sign-in learns it. Each access token is a name: a runner mints a distinct JWT for each, naming who signed in and at which issuer (`email`, `iss`) and expiring an hour from now, or an hour ago when the row lists it in `expired`. A refresh token is its name. Every store each SDK has runs every row, through that SDK's renewal: Go (packages/sdk-go: Issuer.RenewKept, over SignInStore and MemorySignIn, in signinstore_test.go), Python (packages/sdk-python: semiont.http.oauth.renew_kept, over SignInStore and MemorySignIn, in tests/test_sign_in_store.py) and Rust (packages/http-transport-rust: oauth::refresh_stored_session, over SignInStore and InMemorySessionStorage, in tests/sign_in.rs). The launcher renews through Go's (apps/launcher/internal/launcher/session.go), so Go's runner holds it too.

absent.typescript: The TypeScript SDK reads no sign-in store: a TypeScript program signs in by the device grant, and in a browser there is no file to keep one in.

cases.why: elsewhere, XDG_STATE_HOME when it is set
an empty XDG_STATE_HOME is one that is not set
with no home there is no state home, even where XDG_STATE_HOME is set
an empty home is no home
macOS with no home has no state home
Windows follows LOCALAPPDATA where it is not under the home
Windows, when LOCALAPPDATA is not set: where it is by default, under the home
an empty LOCALAPPDATA is one that is not set
Windows with no home has no state home, even where LOCALAPPDATA is set

renewals.why: a renewal keeps what the issuer issued for the refresh token it spent, and gives the new access token
an issuer that rotates no refresh token issues none: the one spent is kept beside the new access token
a renewal another program made while this one's grant was in flight stands: this one's tokens are dropped, and it goes on with the kept access token

at an issuer that rotates no refresh token, another program's renewal during this one's grant leaves the refresh token this one spent, and still stands: what is kept is no longer what this renewal read
another program renewed before this renewal read the store: the kept access token is not the one held and has not expired, so it is given as it is, and no grant is made
another program renewed before this renewal read the store, and the access token it left has expired: the refresh token it left is spent
a renewer that holds no token yet (a session at its start) renews a kept access token that has expired
a stack signed out while the renewal's grant was in flight stays signed out: nothing is written back, and the new access token is given to nobody
a stack signed out before the renewal read the store has nothing to renew: no grant is made, and nothing is given
